newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt state says will privatise 16 firms by June.
newsitem.headline: Egypt state says will privatise 16 firms by June.

text.p: The Egyptian state said on Monday it would privatise 16 companies with a total value of 6.7 billion pounds ($1.97 billion) between April and June 1997.

Egypt's government-owned press quoted Public Enterprise Minister Atef Obeid as saying that the state had also agreed to sell off Helnan Dahab Hotel in the Red Sea resort of Dahab, 16 rice mills, three factories and three cotton ginneries.
He said that the government would initially sell 10 percent tranches in the firms "to test the market".
Government officials regularly give privatisation targets and publish long lists of firms the state intends to sell but these targets are often not met.

In earlier remarks, Obeid said that under the privatisation programme, the state would sell shares in 51 public-sector companies during 1997 -- a lower target than he had given in previous statements.
Some of the 16 firms named by the newspapers on Monday were among other lists published by the state last year.

The firms named include Modern Textiles, Upper Egypt General Contracting, Giza General Contracting, Societe Egyptienne d'Enterprise, Edfina for Preserved Foods, Nasr Preserved Foods/Kaha, Nasr Steel Pipes and Fittings and Egyptian Vineyards/Gianaklis.
